note: Records are written by hand from public sources. Each breach links to the source it is based on. Numbers are the figures given in that source.

breaches.title: 2017 data breach
breaches.affected: About 147 million people
breaches.description: Attackers got into Equifax systems between May and July 2017 and took personal information on about 147 million people. In 2019 Equifax agreed to pay at least $575 million in a settlement with the US Federal Trade Commission, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and US states.

statement.title: Equifax Announces Cybersecurity Incident Involving Consumer Information

outcomes.text: Agreed to pay at least $575 million to the FTC, CFPB and US states

breaches.title: Starwood guest reservation database breach
breaches.affected: Around 339 million guest records worldwide
breaches.description: Attackers got into the reservation systems of Starwood Hotels in 2014, before Marriott bought the company. The breach was not found until 2018. In 2020 the UK Information Commissioner's Office fined Marriott £18.4 million, saying it failed to keep personal data secure.
breaches.source_name: UK Information Commissioner's Office, penalty notice

statement.title: Marriott Announces Starwood Guest Reservation Database Security Incident

outcomes.text: Fined £18.4 million by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: 2018 website payment data theft
breaches.affected: More than 400,000 customers and staff
breaches.description: For about two weeks in August and September 2018, attackers copied payment card details that people typed into the British Airways website. In 2020 the UK Information Commissioner's Office fined the airline £20 million.
breaches.source_name: UK Information Commissioner's Office, penalty notice

outcomes.text: Fined £20 million by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: 2018 UK payment page chatbot attack
breaches.affected: 9.4 million customers across Europe, including 1.5 million in the UK
breaches.description: Attackers compromised a chatbot that was installed on Ticketmaster's online payment page. In November 2020 the UK Information Commissioner's Office fined Ticketmaster UK £1.25 million for not having proper security in place.
breaches.source_name: UK Information Commissioner's Office, annual report 2020/21

outcomes.text: Fined £1.25 million by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: 2024 third-party cloud database breach
breaches.affected: Some customers who bought tickets for North American events
breaches.description: Live Nation told US regulators in May 2024 that it found unauthorised activity in a third-party cloud database containing mostly Ticketmaster data, and that criminals offered what they said was user data for sale. Ticketmaster says the database held limited personal information.

statement.title: Ticketmaster Data Security Incident

breaches.title: Scraped user dataset
breaches.affected: About 533 million users worldwide
breaches.description: This was not a hack of Facebook's servers. People abused Facebook's search and contact-import tools between 2018 and 2019 to collect, or "scrape", profile information, which was later posted online in 2021. In 2022 Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Meta €265 million.

statement.title: The Facts on News Reports About Facebook Data

outcomes.text: Fined €265 million by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission

breaches.title: 2019 cyber incident
breaches.affected: About 100 million people in the US and 6 million in Canada
breaches.description: An outside person used a configuration weakness to take data in March 2019, mostly from people who had applied for Capital One credit cards. Capital One says about 140,000 US Social Security numbers, 80,000 bank account numbers and about 1 million Canadian Social Insurance Numbers were included.

statement.title: 2019 Capital One Cyber Incident

outcomes.text: Class action settlement approved by a US court

breaches.title: 2014 account data theft
breaches.affected: Hundreds of millions of user accounts
breaches.description: Hackers stole data on hundreds of millions of Yahoo accounts in 2014. The US Securities and Exchange Commission said Yahoo did not tell investors for almost two years, and in 2018 the company, then called Altaba, agreed to pay a $35 million penalty.

statement.title: An Important Message to Yahoo Users on Security (filed with the SEC)

outcomes.text: Paid a $35 million penalty to the US Securities and Exchange Commission for not telling investors

breaches.title: 2016 rider and driver data breach
breaches.affected: Tens of millions of riders and drivers
breaches.description: Attackers took rider and driver data in late 2016. The US Federal Trade Commission says Uber did not tell consumers or the FTC about it for more than a year. Uber agreed to an expanded settlement with the FTC in 2018.

statement.title: 2016 Data Security Incident

outcomes.text: Expanded settlement with the US Federal Trade Commission
Fined €600,000 by the Dutch Data Protection Authority for reporting late

breaches.title: 2023 credential stuffing attack
breaches.affected: 155,592 people in the UK, and millions worldwide
breaches.description: Between April and September 2023, an attacker logged in to accounts using passwords leaked in other, unrelated breaches, then reached data shared with relatives. In 2025 the UK Information Commissioner's Office fined 23andMe £2.31 million, pointing to the lack of mandatory two-step login.

statement.title: Addressing Data Security Concerns

outcomes.text: Fined £2.31 million by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: 2021 cyberattack
breaches.affected: About 40 million former or prospective customers and 7.8 million current customers
breaches.description: An attacker got into T-Mobile's systems and took customer data in August 2021. T-Mobile offered two years of free identity protection to people who might be affected. This record covers the 2021 incident only.

statement.title: T-Mobile Cybersecurity Incident Update

breaches.title: 2022 cyberattack
breaches.affected: 9.7 million people (according to the Australian regulator)
breaches.description: An attacker took about 520 gigabytes of data from Australian health insurer Medibank in October 2022. In 2024 the Australian Information Commissioner started civil penalty proceedings, alleging Medibank did not take reasonable steps to protect the data. The court case was still going on when this record was written.
breaches.source_name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

statement.title: Updating our customers about the cybercrime

outcomes.text: Australian Information Commissioner started civil penalty proceedings (ongoing)

breaches.title: 2022 customer data breach
breaches.affected: About 9.5 million people (according to the Australian regulator)
breaches.description: Australian telecom company Optus announced the breach on 22 September 2022. The Australian Information Commissioner has started civil penalty proceedings, alleging Optus did not take reasonable steps to protect personal information. The court case was still going on when this record was written.
breaches.source_name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

statement.title: Optus notifies customers of cyberattack compromising customer information

outcomes.text: Australian Information Commissioner started civil penalty proceedings (ongoing)

breaches.title: Hotel account phishing and late reporting
breaches.affected: More than 4,000 customers
breaches.description: Criminals tricked staff at hotels in the United Arab Emirates into giving up their Booking.com login details and used them to see customer bookings. The Dutch Data Protection Authority fined Booking.com €475,000 in 2021 because it reported the breach 22 days too late.

outcomes.text: Fined €475,000 by the Dutch Data Protection Authority for reporting the breach 22 days late

breaches.title: 2012 password theft
breaches.affected: More than 100 million members
breaches.description: In 2012 about 6.5 million hashed LinkedIn passwords were posted online. In 2016 a much larger set of email and password combinations from the same 2012 theft was released, and LinkedIn reset the passwords of affected accounts.

statement.title: Protecting Our Members

breaches.title: 2013 customer data and source code theft
breaches.affected: About 2.9 million customers' payment records, plus customer IDs and encrypted passwords
breaches.description: Adobe announced in October 2013 that attackers had taken customer IDs and encrypted passwords, plus payment information on about 2.9 million customers. Adobe said it did not believe decrypted card numbers were taken. Source code for several Adobe products was also accessed.

statement.title: Important Customer Security Announcement

breaches.title: Call and text records from 2022 downloaded from a cloud platform
breaches.affected: Nearly all AT&T cellular customers
breaches.description: AT&T said in July 2024 that records of calls and texts from May to October 2022 were illegally downloaded from a workspace on a third-party cloud platform. The records show which numbers customers contacted, not the content of calls or texts, and do not include names, but names can often be looked up from phone numbers.

statement.title: AT&T Addresses Illegal Download of Customer Data

breaches.title: Customer data set released on the dark web
breaches.affected: About 7.6 million current and 65.4 million former account holders
breaches.description: In March 2024 AT&T confirmed that a data set found on the dark web contained AT&T-specific information, believed to be from 2019 or earlier. AT&T said it had not yet determined whether the data came from AT&T or one of its vendors, and reset passcodes for affected current customers.

statement.title: AT&T Addresses Recent Data Set Released on the Dark Web

breaches.title: 2024 ransomware attack
breaches.affected: About 190 million people (later updated to about 192.7 million)
breaches.description: A ransomware attack on Change Healthcare, a UnitedHealth Group company that processes US medical claims, disrupted healthcare payments across the US in February 2024. It became the largest health data breach reported to US regulators.
breaches.source_name: US Department of Health and Human Services

statement.title: UnitedHealth Group Update on Change Healthcare Cyberattack

outcomes.text: Investigated by the US health regulator (HHS Office for Civil Rights)

breaches.title: 2025 customer service vendor breach
breaches.affected: Users who contacted Discord support, including about 70,000 whose ID photos may have been exposed
categories: Partial payment card details (last four digits, some)
breaches.description: An attacker broke into a third-party customer service provider used by Discord and accessed data from users who had contacted support or Trust and Safety, including ID photos submitted for age checks. Discord says its own systems were not breached and it stopped working with the vendor.

statement.title: Update on a Security Incident Involving Third-Party Customer Service

breaches.title: 2025 insider data theft and extortion attempt
breaches.affected: Less than 1% of Coinbase's monthly transacting users
categories: Partial Social Security numbers (last four digits)
breaches.description: Criminals paid a small group of overseas customer support workers to copy customer data, then tried to extort Coinbase for $20 million. Coinbase refused to pay, fired the workers and said it would reimburse customers tricked into sending money. Passwords, private keys and funds were not accessed.

statement.title: Protecting Our Customers - Standing Up to Extortionists

breaches.title: 2025 contact centre platform breach
breaches.affected: 5.7 million customers
breaches.description: A cyber criminal accessed a third-party customer service platform used by a Qantas contact centre. Qantas says passwords, PINs, credit card details and passport details were not accessed, and it got a court order to stop the stolen data being published.

statement.title: Update on Qantas cyber incident: Wednesday 9 July 2025

breaches.title: 2023 loyalty program database theft
breaches.affected: A significant number of Caesars Rewards members
breaches.description: Attackers used social engineering on an outsourced IT support vendor to get into Caesars' network and copy its loyalty program database. Caesars offered credit monitoring to all loyalty members.

statement.title: Caesars Entertainment Form 8-K, September 2023

breaches.title: 2023 cyberattack
breaches.affected: Some MGM Resorts customers
breaches.description: A September 2023 cyberattack forced MGM to shut down systems at its US casinos and hotels for days. MGM says the attackers took personal information for some customers, but not passwords, bank account numbers or payment card details.

statement.title: MGM Resorts Form 8-K, October 2023

breaches.title: 2023 support system breach
breaches.affected: All users of Okta's customer support system, and files of 134 customers
breaches.description: An attacker used a stolen service account to access Okta's customer support system and downloaded files from 134 customers, some containing session tokens used to hijack sessions. Okta later found the attacker also downloaded the names and email addresses of all support system users.

statement.title: Unauthorized Access to Okta's Support Case Management System: Root Cause and Remediation

breaches.title: 2022 cloud backup and vault data theft
breaches.affected: LastPass customers whose data was in the stolen backups
breaches.description: After an earlier break-in at a developer environment, an attacker copied backups containing customer account information and encrypted password vault data. Vault contents can only be unlocked with each user's master password, which LastPass does not store, but weak master passwords could be guessed.

statement.title: Security Incident December 2022 Update

breaches.title: Account lookup vulnerability
breaches.affected: About 5.4 million accounts (reported)
breaches.description: A bug introduced in 2021 let someone enter an email address or phone number and find out which Twitter account it belonged to. Attackers used it to build a list of accounts linked to private emails and phone numbers. Twitter fixed the bug in January 2022 and confirmed the incident in August 2022.

statement.title: An incident impacting some accounts and private information on Twitter

breaches.title: Google+ profile API bug
breaches.affected: About 52.5 million Google+ users
breaches.description: Bugs in a Google+ API could let apps see profile fields that users had not made public. Google said it found no evidence the data was misused, and it shut down consumer Google+ early as a result.

statement.title: Expediting changes to Google+

breaches.title: 2012 credentials theft
breaches.affected: About 68 million users
breaches.description: Dropbox announced in July 2012 that a stolen employee password had been used to access a document with user email addresses. In 2016 it learned the 2012 theft also included about 68 million email addresses with hashed passwords, and reset passwords for users who had not changed them since mid-2012.

statement.title: Resetting passwords to keep your files safe

breaches.title: 2019 user database breach
breaches.affected: Up to 139 million users
breaches.description: An attacker accessed Canva's user profile data in May 2019. Passwords were hashed with bcrypt, but Canva later said about 4 million passwords were cracked, and it reset passwords for users who had not changed them.

statement.title: Canva Security Incident

breaches.title: 2015 user database breach
breaches.affected: Slack users at the time (passwords reset for about 1% of accounts in 2019)
breaches.description: Attackers got into a Slack database with usernames and hashed passwords in 2015, and inserted code to capture passwords as people typed them. In 2019 Slack reset the passwords of accounts active at the time as a precaution.

statement.title: New information about Slack's 2015 security incident

breaches.title: 2025 lab hack affecting the cervical cancer screening programme
breaches.affected: Up to about 941,000 participants in the Dutch cervical cancer screening programme
breaches.description: Hackers broke into Clinical Diagnostics NMDL, a Dutch laboratory that analysed tests for the national cervical cancer screening programme. Bevolkingsonderzoek Nederland first reported about 485,000 affected participants, later decided to write to all 941,000 people whose data it had shared with the lab, and stopped using the lab. The Dutch Data Protection Authority started an investigation.

statement.title: Datalek veel groter dan eerder vermeld (Bevolkingsonderzoek Nederland)

outcomes.text: Investigated by the Dutch Data Protection Authority and the Health and Youth Care Inspectorate

breaches.title: 2022 US customer data breach
breaches.affected: Some Samsung customers in the US
breaches.description: An unauthorised third party took information from some of Samsung's US systems in late July 2022. Samsung says Social Security numbers and credit or debit card numbers were not affected.

statement.title: An important notice regarding U.S. customer information

breaches.title: 2021 source code and creator payout leak
breaches.affected: A small fraction of users, mainly streamers
breaches.description: A server configuration error let an outsider copy Twitch's source code and a subset of creator payout data, which was then posted online. Twitch says passwords, full card numbers and bank details were not exposed.

statement.title: Updates on the Twitch Security Incident

breaches.title: 2022 user database breach
breaches.affected: Plex account holders (all were asked to reset passwords)
breaches.description: An outsider accessed a Plex database containing emails, usernames and hashed passwords. Plex says it does not store card data, and required all users to reset their passwords.

statement.title: Important notice of a potential data breach (24 August 2022)

breaches.title: 2013 holiday payment card theft
breaches.affected: About 40 million payment cards, plus contact details of up to 70 million people
breaches.description: Malware on checkout terminals in Target's US stores captured card data between 27 November and 15 December 2013. Target later said contact details of up to 70 million people were also taken.

statement.title: Target Confirms Unauthorized Access to Payment Card Data in U.S. Stores

breaches.title: 2014 payment card malware
breaches.affected: About 56 million payment cards and 53 million email addresses
breaches.description: Custom-built malware on self-checkout systems in US and Canadian stores captured card details between April and September 2014. Home Depot later said files with about 53 million email addresses were also taken.

statement.title: The Home Depot Completes Malware Elimination and Enhanced Encryption of Payment Data in All U.S. Stores

breaches.title: 2018 account data breach
breaches.affected: About 150 million accounts
breaches.description: An unauthorised party took MyFitnessPal account data in February 2018, while the app was owned by Under Armour. Most passwords were hashed with bcrypt, and users were asked to change them.

statement.title: Under Armour Notifies MyFitnessPal Users Of Data Security Issue

breaches.title: 2014 user database breach
breaches.affected: eBay users worldwide (all were asked to change passwords)
breaches.description: Attackers used a few stolen employee logins to reach a database of customer details between late February and early March 2014. eBay asked every user to change their password and said financial data was stored separately and not accessed.

statement.title: eBay Inc. To Ask eBay Users To Change Passwords

breaches.title: 2025 cyberattack
breaches.affected: Some M&S customers
breaches.description: A cyberattack in April 2025 forced M&S to pause online orders for weeks. M&S says some customer data was taken, but not usable card details or account passwords, and expected the attack to cost around £300 million.

statement.title: Cyber Update

breaches.title: Breach of historic online orders (2018–2020)
breaches.affected: About 10 million customers
categories: Partial payment card details (last four digits)
breaches.description: In January 2023 JD Sports said attackers accessed a system holding online orders from November 2018 to October 2020 for its JD, Size?, Millets, Blacks, Scotts and MilletSport brands. It does not hold full card details and found no sign that passwords were accessed.

statement.title: Cyber security incident regarding historic orders

breaches.title: 2018 US website data breach
breaches.affected: Certain adidas consumers (US website)
breaches.description: In June 2018 adidas said an unauthorised party claimed to have obtained limited data about some consumers who used its US website. adidas said it had no reason to believe card or fitness data was affected.

statement.title: adidas alerts certain consumers of potential data security incident

breaches.title: 2015 breach of T-Mobile credit application data (2013–2015 applicants)
breaches.affected: About 15 million people who applied for T-Mobile US services
breaches.description: A hacker took records from an Experian server that processed credit checks for T-Mobile US, covering applicants from September 2013 to September 2015. Social Security and ID numbers were encrypted, but Experian believed the encryption may have been compromised.

breaches.title: 2015 cyberattack
breaches.affected: Almost 79 million people
breaches.description: Attackers got in through phishing emails and stole data between December 2014 and January 2015, in what was then the largest health data breach in US history. In 2018 Anthem paid a record $16 million to settle with the US health regulator.
breaches.source_name: US Department of Health and Human Services

outcomes.text: Paid a record $16 million to settle with the US health regulator (HHS)

breaches.title: 2023 cyberattack
breaches.affected: About 14 million customers and applicants in Australia and New Zealand
categories: Bank account and card numbers (some, mostly closed)
breaches.description: An attacker used credentials stolen from a vendor to take data on current and past customers and applicants. About 7.9 million driver's licence numbers were among it. Latitude refused to pay a ransom.

statement.title: Cybercrime Update

breaches.title: 2024 third-party database breach
breaches.affected: Customers in Chile, Spain and Uruguay, plus current and some former employees
breaches.description: Santander said someone accessed a Santander database hosted by a third-party provider. It says the database held no transaction data or login details such as online banking passwords, and customers in other countries were not affected.

statement.title: Statement (Banco Santander, May 2024)

breaches.title: Connected car data left on a public cloud server
breaches.affected: About 2.15 million customers in Japan
breaches.description: A cloud server holding data from Toyota's connected car services in Japan was mistakenly set to public, leaving vehicle and location data accessible for about ten years until 2023. Toyota said it had not confirmed any misuse of the data.

statement.title: Apology and Notice Concerning Newly Discovered Potential Data Leakage of Customer Information Due to Cloud Settings

outcomes.text: Received guidance from Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission

breaches.title: 2024 student information system breach
breaches.affected: Students and teachers at many US and Canadian schools
categories: Social Security or Social Insurance numbers (some)
breaches.description: An attacker used one stolen login to reach PowerSchool's customer support portal and copy student and teacher data from schools using its student information system. PowerSchool says no card or banking data was involved and offered identity protection.

statement.title: PowerSchool Cybersecurity Incident

breaches.title: 2021 customer support social engineering attack
breaches.affected: About 5 million email addresses and 2 million names
categories: Dates of birth and ZIP codes (a few hundred)
breaches.description: An attacker tricked a customer support employee by phone and got into support systems, then demanded a ransom. Robinhood says no Social Security, bank account or card numbers were exposed.

statement.title: Robinhood Announces Data Security Incident (Update)

breaches.title: Former employee downloaded investing reports
breaches.affected: About 8.2 million current and former US customers
breaches.description: A former employee downloaded Cash App Investing reports after their job ended. Block says the reports did not include usernames, passwords, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, card details, addresses or bank account information.

statement.title: Block Form 8-K, April 2022

breaches.title: 2020 e-commerce and marketing database breach
breaches.affected: About 292,000 customers' full details and more than 1 million email addresses
breaches.description: An attacker used a third-party API key to access Ledger's e-commerce and marketing database. The data was later published online, leading to phishing and threats against crypto wallet owners. Ledger says wallets and funds were not affected.

statement.title: Addressing the July 2020 e-commerce and marketing data breach

breaches.title: Repeated breaches from 2017 to 2020
breaches.affected: About 40 million users and employees
categories: Scholarship data (religion, ethnicity, date of birth, income)
breaches.description: The US Federal Trade Commission said Chegg's careless security led to four breaches, including one where a former contractor used shared login details to access data on about 40 million customers. Chegg agreed to an FTC order in 2023.

outcomes.text: Ordered by the US Federal Trade Commission to overhaul its data security

breaches.title: 2025 customer service platform breach
breaches.affected: Some Air France and KLM customers
breaches.description: Air France and KLM found unusual activity on an external platform used for customer service, where someone accessed customer data. They say internal systems were not affected and no passwords, travel details, miles, passport or card details were taken. KLM reported it to the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

statement.title: KLM informeert klanten over incident met persoonsgegevens

breaches.title: 2024 subscriber data theft
breaches.affected: Data from 24 million subscriber contracts
breaches.description: An attacker got into the systems of French telecom operators Free and Free Mobile in October 2024 and accessed subscriber data, including bank account numbers for some customers. In 2026 France's data protection authority, the CNIL, fined the two companies €42 million.

outcomes.text: Fined €42 million by France’s data protection authority (CNIL)

breaches.title: 2023 internal tool breach
breaches.affected: 133 Mailchimp business accounts
breaches.description: Attackers used social engineering on Mailchimp staff to get into an internal customer support tool and reach 133 customer accounts, some belonging to crypto companies. It was Mailchimp's third similar incident in under a year.

statement.title: Information About a Recent Security Incident

breaches.title: 2022 SMS phishing attack on employees
breaches.affected: 209 customer accounts and 93 Authy users
breaches.description: Attackers sent fake text messages to Twilio employees and used stolen logins to reach internal tools and data from some customer accounts. Some of that data was then used to target users of apps like Signal.

statement.title: Incident Report: Employee and Customer Account Compromise

breaches.title: 2021 Managed WordPress breach
breaches.affected: Up to 1.2 million Managed WordPress customers
breaches.description: Using a stolen password, an attacker got into GoDaddy's Managed WordPress system in September 2021 and went unnoticed until November. GoDaddy reset the exposed passwords and reissued certificates.

statement.title: GoDaddy blog post on the data security incident (filed with the SEC)

breaches.title: 2020 Nintendo Network ID account takeovers
breaches.affected: About 300,000 accounts
breaches.description: Attackers logged into Nintendo Network IDs using passwords stolen elsewhere, and some used linked Nintendo Accounts to buy items. Nintendo says its own servers were not breached and no card data was exposed. It ended NNID sign-in to Nintendo Accounts and refunded fraudulent purchases.

statement.title: 「ニンテンドーネットワークID」に対する不正ログイン発生のご報告

breaches.title: Leak of a 2019 copy of user data kept by a former partner
breaches.affected: Deezer users whose data was held by the former partner
breaches.description: In 2022 Deezer learned that a service provider it stopped working with in 2020 had kept a 2019 copy of user data instead of deleting it, and that copy was hacked. Deezer says its own systems were not affected and no passwords or payment details were exposed.

statement.title: Third Party Data Breach

breaches.title: 2025 cloud system breach
breaches.affected: Allianz Life customers, financial professionals and some employees in the US
breaches.description: On 16 July 2025 an attacker accessed a cloud-based system used by the US insurer Allianz Life. Allianz says there is no evidence its own network or other systems were accessed.

statement.title: Notice of Data Security Incident (sample letter)

breaches.title: 2025 customer account exposure
breaches.affected: About 33.7 million customer accounts in South Korea
breaches.description: Using a stolen internal security key, a former employee accessed South Korean customer accounts from June 2025, going unnoticed until November. Coupang says payment details, logins and ID documents were not accessed, and offered vouchers to every affected customer.

statement.title: Update on the November 29 personal information incident

breaches.title: 2025 USIM data hack
breaches.affected: About 23 million subscribers (according to South Korea's privacy regulator)
breaches.description: Malware planted on SK Telecom's systems let hackers take SIM card data that could be used to clone SIMs. SK Telecom offered free SIM replacements, and in 2025 South Korea's privacy regulator fined it a record 134.8 billion won, which SK Telecom is appealing.

statement.title: SK Telecom Announces Accountability and Commitment Program

outcomes.text: Fined a record 134.8 billion won by South Korea’s privacy regulator (being appealed)

breaches.title: 2025 customer data cyberattack
breaches.affected: 6.4 million customer accounts
breaches.description: French telecom operator Bouygues Telecom detected a cyberattack on 4 August 2025 that exposed personal data from 6.4 million customer accounts. It says passwords and card numbers were not affected, and it reported the attack to the CNIL and the police.

statement.title: Bouygues Telecom, victime d'une cyberattaque

breaches.title: 2025 cyberattack
breaches.affected: About 850,000 customer accounts
breaches.description: Orange Belgium found a cyberattack on one of its IT systems at the end of July 2025. It says no passwords, email addresses or bank details were taken. Leaked PUK codes can help fraudsters take over phone numbers.

statement.title: Orange Belgium informs its customers about a cyberattack

breaches.title: 2025 customer support application breach
breaches.affected: About 4.4 million US consumers
breaches.description: An attacker used social engineering to get into a third-party application used by TransUnion's customer support. TransUnion says its core credit database was not affected and offered affected consumers credit monitoring.

breaches.title: 2026 customer data hack
breaches.affected: 6.2 million customer accounts of Odido and Ben (according to Odido)
breaches.description: Hackers got into Odido's customer database by phishing customer service staff and pretending to be the IT department. Odido refused to pay and the criminals published the data. The Dutch Data Protection Authority is also looking at whether Odido kept former customers' data too long.

outcomes.text: Investigated by the Dutch Data Protection Authority over how long it kept customer data

breaches.title: 2024 Midnight Blizzard email hack
breaches.affected: A small share of Microsoft corporate email accounts, including senior leadership
breaches.description: A Russian state-sponsored group got into a test account through password spraying, then read corporate email of senior leaders and security and legal staff. Microsoft later said the group used the stolen information to try to get into source code and internal systems.

statement.title: Microsoft Actions Following Attack by Nation State Actor Midnight Blizzard

breaches.title: 2019 hack of internal systems
breaches.affected: About 83,000 people whose data was downloaded
breaches.description: A hacker got into Transavia’s systems in September 2019 through two IT accounts that had easy-to-guess passwords and no two-step login. Data on about 83,000 people was downloaded, including medical details such as wheelchair use for 367 passengers. The hacker could in principle reach data on about 25 million people. The Dutch Data Protection Authority fined Transavia €400,000 in 2021.

outcomes.text: Fined €400,000 by the Dutch Data Protection Authority for poor security

breaches.title: 2015 cyber attack
breaches.affected: 156,959 customers
breaches.description: Attackers used a well-known technique (SQL injection) on old web pages TalkTalk had inherited when it bought Tiscali’s UK business. They took personal details of 156,959 customers, and bank details of 15,656 of them. The UK Information Commissioner’s Office said the attack could have been prevented and fined TalkTalk a record £400,000 in 2016.

outcomes.text: Fined £400,000 by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: Passenger data breach found in 2018
breaches.affected: About 9.4 million passengers worldwide
breaches.description: Cathay Pacific’s systems lacked proper security from October 2014 to May 2018, and attackers got into them. Database backups were not encrypted, against the airline’s own policy. About 9.4 million passengers were affected. The UK Information Commissioner’s Office fined the airline £500,000 in 2020, the most it could under the law at the time.
breaches.source_name: UK Information Commissioner’s Office, penalty notice

outcomes.text: Fined £500,000 by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: Malware on shop tills
breaches.affected: At least 14 million people, including 5.6 million payment cards
categories: Payment card numbers and expiry dates
breaches.description: Hackers installed malware on 5,390 tills in Currys PC World and Dixons Travel shops between July 2017 and April 2018. The UK Information Commissioner’s Office blamed weak security, such as missing patches and firewalls, and fined the company £500,000 in 2020. After years of appeals the case ended in 2026 with the company agreeing to pay £200,000.

outcomes.text: Fined £500,000 by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office
A tribunal cut the fine to £250,000; the case then went through further appeals
Agreed to pay £200,000 to end the case

breaches.title: 2023 ransomware attack
breaches.affected: 6.6 million people
categories: Health and other sensitive information (some people)
breaches.description: Ransomware attackers got into Capita’s network in March 2023 and stole personal information of 6.6 million people, much of it from pension schemes Capita runs for employers. A high-priority security alert went unanswered for 58 hours. The UK Information Commissioner’s Office fined Capita £14 million in 2025, and Capita accepted the fine.

outcomes.text: Fined £14 million by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: 2024 cyberattack on US systems
breaches.affected: About 2.2 million people, mostly current and former US employees
breaches.description: In November 2024 attackers got into some of Ahold Delhaize’s US business systems. In April 2025 the company confirmed that files had been taken, mainly employment records. A notice filed with US authorities put the number of people affected at about 2.2 million. The company said customer payment and pharmacy systems were not affected.

statement.title: Update on Ahold Delhaize’s cybersecurity incident

breaches.title: 2022 social engineering attack
breaches.affected: 50,150 customers worldwide
breaches.description: In September 2022 an attacker tricked their way into a Revolut database. Details of 50,150 customers were exposed, about 20,000 of them in Europe. Revolut said card numbers, PINs and passwords were not accessed. Lithuania’s data protection authority, Revolut’s lead regulator in the EU, opened an investigation.
breaches.source_name: State Data Protection Inspectorate of Lithuania

outcomes.text: Lithuania’s data protection authority opened an investigation

breaches.title: 2018 attack on the mobile banking portal
breaches.affected: About 778,000 customers and former customers in Italy
breaches.description: In 2018 an attack on UniCredit’s mobile banking portal exposed names, tax ID numbers and customer codes of about 778,000 current and former customers. Italy’s data protection authority fined the bank €2.8 million in 2024. UniCredit said no banking data was affected and that it would challenge the fine in court.
breaches.source_name: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italian Data Protection Authority)

outcomes.text: Fined €2.8 million by the Italian Data Protection Authority (UniCredit is appealing)

breaches.title: 2024 attack on a health insurance payment platform
breaches.affected: Part of more than 33 million people affected across Viamedis and Almerys
breaches.description: Viamedis handles payments between French health insurers and pharmacies, doctors and hospitals. In early 2024 attackers broke into its systems, and around the same time into those of Almerys, which does the same work. France’s data protection authority said more than 33 million people were affected across the two. It said contact details and bank details were not involved.

outcomes.text: France’s data protection authority opened an investigation

breaches.title: 2024 attack on a health insurance payment platform
breaches.affected: Part of more than 33 million people affected across Almerys and Viamedis
breaches.description: Almerys handles payments between French health insurers and healthcare providers. In February 2024 attackers broke into its systems, shortly after a similar attack on Viamedis. France’s data protection authority said more than 33 million people were affected across the two. It said contact details and bank details were not involved.

outcomes.text: France’s data protection authority opened an investigation

breaches.title: 2023 theft of payment card data
breaches.affected: Not disclosed
breaches.description: Between August and September 2023 attackers took payment card details, including security codes, from Air Europa’s online sales system. The airline emailed affected customers in October and told them to cancel their cards. It later said some customers’ names, ID or passport numbers and frequent flyer codes may also have been exposed. It never said how many people were affected.

breaches.title: 2015 hack and leak of user data
breaches.affected: More than 36 million users
breaches.description: Hackers broke into the dating site in July 2015 and published profile, account and billing details of more than 36 million users a month later. Some had paid for a ‘full delete’ of their profile that didn’t fully remove their data. In 2016 the operators settled with the US Federal Trade Commission and 13 states, agreeing to pay $1.6 million.

outcomes.text: Agreed to pay $1.6 million to the FTC and US states

breaches.title: 2023 breach through a Citrix flaw
breaches.affected: About 35.9 million customers
categories: Last four digits of Social Security numbers
breaches.description: Between 16 and 19 October 2023 attackers used a known flaw in Citrix software to get into Xfinity’s systems. Usernames and scrambled (hashed) passwords were taken, and for some customers also names, contact details, birth dates, partial Social Security numbers and security questions. Xfinity made customers reset their passwords. A filing with US authorities put the number affected at about 35.9 million.

statement.title: Notice To Customers of Data Security Incident

breaches.title: 2011 PlayStation Network hack
breaches.affected: About 77 million accounts
breaches.description: Between 17 and 19 April 2011 attackers broke into Sony’s PlayStation Network and Qriocity services and took account details. Sony shut the network down for weeks. It said it had no evidence card data was taken but couldn’t rule it out. In 2013 the UK Information Commissioner’s Office fined Sony £250,000, saying the attack could have been prevented.

statement.title: Update on PlayStation Network and Qriocity

outcomes.text: Fined £250,000 by the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

breaches.title: Exposed location data of electric cars
breaches.affected: About 800,000 electric cars, with precise locations for about 460,000
breaches.description: Volkswagen’s software company Cariad left a cloud storage system open to the internet. It held months of location data from about 800,000 electric cars from Volkswagen, Audi, Skoda and Seat, linked to owners’ contact details. A tip-off reached the Chaos Computer Club, which warned Volkswagen in November 2024 and went public in December. Volkswagen blamed a configuration mistake and closed the gap.

breaches.title: 2020 cyber attack
breaches.affected: About 9 million customers, with card details of 2,208
breaches.description: easyJet learned of a cyber attack in January 2020 and announced it in May. The attacker saw email addresses and travel details of about 9 million customers, and card details of 2,208 of them. The UK Information Commissioner’s Office investigated and closed the case in 2023 without taking action. A group legal claim by customers was filed in 2020.

outcomes.text: The UK Information Commissioner’s Office investigated and closed the case without action
